text:
Vasily Podkolzin came to Edmonton as a former Canucks first-rounder who hadn't found his spot. This fall he has found plenty: 10 goals and 16 points in 22 games, a bump to 17:20 a night, and a piece of the power play (on the ice for 39% of the Oilers' chances, up from 12%). His own chances are up too, to 1.21 expected goals per 60 (a measure of shot quality) from 0.78, so the improvement isn't invented.

But the finish is running hot. He's shooting 22.2%, well above his usual range, and the Oilers have scored about 11 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Those are the two numbers most likely to cool. There are signs it already has: three points in his last ten games, at 15:10 a night, nearly four minutes below his season average. What should hold is the possession side. Edmonton gets 61% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him out there, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries last season, the habit that creates chances rather than hoping for them.
